title: Dative 1: To Whom? (All Three Genders)
description: The dative case answers 'Кому?' (To whom?). Today: singular dative endings for masculine, feminine, and neuter nouns.
descriptionRussian: Дательный падеж отвечает на вопрос 'Кому?'. Сегодня: окончания дательного падежа для мужского, женского и среднего рода в единственном числе.
intro: The dative marks whoever is on the receiving end: the person you give something to, write to, or help. English handles that with a small word or with word order, and Russian handles it with an ending. What makes this case bigger than it looks is where else it turns up. By lesson 5 you will be using it to say your age and to say that you are cold.
rules: The dative case (дательный падеж) marks the RECIPIENT or ADDRESSEE of an action. It answers the question 'Кому?' (To whom?).
Masculine consonant nouns add -у in the dative: брат → брату, друг → другу, Антон → Антону.
Feminine nouns ending in -а or -я swap the final vowel for -е: мама → маме, школа → школе, тётя → тёте.
Neuter nouns ending in -о swap -о for -у; nouns ending in -е swap -е for -ю: окно → окну, письмо → письму, море → морю.
Important: the feminine dative -е coincides with the feminine prepositional -е. Context (the verb and any preposition) tells you which case is in play.
examples: Я помогаю брату. (I help brother.) брат → брату.
Маша звонит маме. (Masha is calling mom.) мама → маме.
Антон помогает тёте. (Anton helps aunt.) тётя → тёте.
Я звоню Антону. (I'm calling Anton.) Антон → Антону.
Маша рада письму. (Masha is glad about the letter.) письмо → письму.
Антон рад морю. (Anton is glad about the sea.) море → морю.

items.hint: What ending does a masculine consonant noun take in the dative?
items.explanation: Помогать takes a dative complement: помогать кому. Брат is masculine consonant, so it adds -у in the dative: брату.

items.hint: Feminine -а changes to which letter in the dative?
items.explanation: Звонить takes a dative complement: звонить кому. Мама is feminine -а: -а → -е → маме. The form looks the same as the prepositional 'я думаю о маме,' but the trigger here is the verb звонить, not the preposition о.

items.hint: Feminine -я follows the same dative pattern as feminine -а.
items.explanation: Тётя ends in -я. Feminine -я swaps to -е, parallel to feminine -а → -е. Тётя → тёте. The soft -я ending stays soft as -е.

items.hint: Антон is a masculine consonant name. Apply the masculine rule.
items.explanation: Names follow the same rules as common nouns. Антон is masculine consonant: + -у → Антону.

Сестра is feminine -а: -а → -е → сестре. Feminine dative is identical in form to feminine prepositional, but the role is different: here сестре is the recipient of help, not the topic of conversation.

items.hint: Друг is masculine consonant. Recall Q1.1's pattern.
items.explanation: Друг → другу. Masculine consonant + -у. By the end of this lesson the masculine pattern should feel automatic: брату, другу, Антону, сыну.

blanks: Маша рада _____. (Masha is glad about the letter.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Письмо is neuter -о. The construction 'рад/рада чему' (glad about something) takes the dative: -о → -у → письму.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша часто помогает дедушка с компьютером.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha often helps her grandpa with the computer.
errorCorrection.explanation: Помогать governs the dative: the person you help goes in the dative. Дедушка ends in -а, so it declines like a feminine -а noun even though it is masculine: дедушке.
Звонить governs the dative: the person you call goes in the dative, so бабушка → бабушке (feminine -а swaps to -е). The bare nominative бабушка can only be a subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон очень рад письмо от друга.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton is very glad about the letter from his friend.
errorCorrection.explanation: The short adjective рад ('glad') governs the dative: рад чему. Письмо is neuter ending in -о, so the dative swaps -о for -у: письму.

minimalPairs.explanation: After помогать (to help), the noun shifts into the dative: брату. The nominative брат would only appear as a subject: 'Брат работает' (Brother is working).

After звонить (to call), the noun shifts into the dative: маме. The same form маме also appears in the prepositional 'я думаю о маме,' but the trigger differs: звонить takes the dative directly, while 'о' triggers the prepositional.

reviewVocab.definition: dative case (marks the recipient or addressee of an action; answers 'Кому?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я помогаю брату' слово 'брату' стоит в дательном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: to help (the person being helped goes in the dative: помогать кому)
